title: Lighthouse of Alexandria (Pharos)
summary: The Pharos was a lighthouse built on the island of Pharos at the entrance to Alexandria's harbour in Egypt, c. 300–280 BCE under Ptolemy I and II. Modern estimates of its height run from 100 to 140 m. Earthquakes damaged it repeatedly, and one account says a quake in 1375 reduced what stood to rubble; Sultan Qaitbay later built a fort on its foundation.

uncertainty.note: Start is c. 300 BCE (astronomical -299) from World History Encyclopedia, which gives c. 300–280 BCE; the Suda date of 297 BC and Eusebius dates of 284/283 BC are in the Chicago page. End is 1375, when the Chicago page says an earthquake seems finally to have reduced the remains to rubble; World History Encyclopedia puts the final collapse in the 1330s and the Muslim Heritage page cites 1365 (Vrettos), so the end is uncertain.

phases.description: Begun by Ptolemy I and completed some 20 years later by Ptolemy II (c. 300-280 BCE).
The pages opened record no damage before the earthquake of AD 796.
The 796 earthquake left only the square section standing; a wooden cupola was built on top in about AD 875; earthquakes in 950/951 and 955/956 threw down about thirty cubits.
A destructive tremor in 1303 that al-Mansuri said destroyed the Pharos; by 1349 it was too ruinous to enter.

An earthquake in 1375 seems finally to have reduced the remains to rubble; in 1479 Sultan Qaitbay used the stones for a fort on its foundation. Other pages date the final collapse to the 1330s or 1365.

reviewer_note: Shape tower; the real form was three stages, so a plain tower is an approximation. Confidence contested: height estimates run 100-200 m across pages (World History Encyclopedia 100-140; Muslim Heritage 103-118 or 140-183); I used the 122 m of the 1195 measurement from the Chicago page. The 30 x 30 m base is a modern scholar (McKenzie) quoted on Muslim Heritage, a non-institutional site (class other). Destruction date differs by page (1303 damage, 1330s, 1365, 1375); I used 1375 from Chicago. Coordinates are the Qaitbay Citadel, which the Chicago page says stands on the Pharos foundation.
